key_insight: Learned UNet and transformer surrogates emulate 3D resistive MHD turbulence with relative velocity errors of 0.018–0.053 while preserving key flow structures and statistics over about one large-eddy turnover time.
engineering_relevance: These surrogates offer a potential route to less costly plasma-flow modeling relevant to astrophysics and fusion, though deployment speedups are not quantified in the abstract.
method: Compare a convolutional UNet, shifted-window transformer and Fourier neural operator as autoregressive emulators.
Train on 128³ decaying MHD simulations at Reynolds numbers 1000, 3000 and 6000.
Use single-step training followed by short-rollout training, with a shared stopping rule.
evidence_signal: Training uses 500 simulations per Reynolds number; public-benchmark evaluations report 39% lower error than the best published FactFormer isotropic-turbulence model and rollout errors one-third to one-half below The Well’s best baselines.
watch_item: Long-horizon stability and generalization beyond the studied resolutions, Reynolds numbers and benchmark conditions remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Learned Surrogates of Three-Dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic Turbulence
